newsitem.title: USA: IMF wants Russia to open govt debt market - sources.
newsitem.headline: IMF wants Russia to open govt debt market - sources.

text.p: International Monetary Fund board members urged Russia to further open up its government securities market to foreigners at a meeting last week, international monetary sources said on Tuesday.

The sources, who declined to be named, called Moscow's restrictions on foreign access to the market counter-productive because they rob Russia of badly-needed capital and keep its interest rates high.
Moscow liberalized access to the market last month. One source called that a step forward but said more needed to be done.
Russian officials at the meeting agreed that the current system was not ideal and told the board that Moscow planned to push ahead with further reforms, according to the sources.
The officials explained though that Russia wants to avoid a volatile government securities market that is particularly susceptible to sudden selling by foreigners.
At the meeting on Friday, the IMF board approved the release of roughly $350 million in additional credits to Russia, saying that its reform program remained on track.
